A caller who commits a trojanised binary at that path can cause the workflow to execute an attacker-controlled Conftest binary that fabricates policy findings (e.g., returns all-allow), completely neutralising policy enforcement.","evidence":"resolve_conftest() at policy-check.yml lines 128-145 has three resolution paths: (1) download+SHA256 verify, (2) vendored archive+SHA256 verify, (3) plain vendored binary vendor/conftest/conftest with no integrity check whatsoever (lines 140-142: 'if [ -f \"${vendored_binary}\" ]; then printf \"%s\\n\" \"${vendored_binary}\"; return 0; fi'). By contrast OPA receives gh attestation verify after SHA256 (line 151). Conftest has no Sigstore attestation call at all. Any commit that places a file at vendor/conftest/conftest bypasses both SHA256 and Sigstore verification and is executed as the policy engine. The Conftest binary produces the policy-findings.json that all downstream steps — threshold enforcement, bypass gate, conflict gate, summary artefact — depend on for correctness.","impact":"A caller repo (or a compromised Codex dispatch during 020C or later) that commits vendor/conftest/conftest with a malicious binary causes every policy check run in that repo to return a fabricated verdict. The binary can emit all-allow findings, suppressing every SCP-R-NNN deny. The SHA256 hash hardcoded in the workflow matches the legitimate Conftest release, so the lack of verification on the vendor binary path is invisible in the workflow YAML. The required check (scp/policy-check) passes. All downstream estate repos that adopt this workflow inherit the same vulnerability if they commit a vendor/ directory. This undermines the entire security invariant of 020B.","mitigation":"Remove the plain-binary vendor fallback (lines 140-142). The two safe fallback paths (download+SHA256 and vendored-archive+SHA256) are sufficient. If an offline vendor binary is needed, require it to be the .tar.gz archive with verified SHA256 — never a bare executable. Additionally add gh attestation verify for Conftest once Conftest publishes Sigstore attestations (track at open-policy-agent/conftest); until then add a compensating comment in the workflow explaining why Sigstore is absent and that the bare-binary vendor path is disabled."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"verify-bypass-pairing.sh validates that waivers.json contains the bypass rule_id and that the entry appears as an added diff line, but never checks that expires_at is in the future. An expired waiver — or a waiver with expires_at: '2021-01-01' — fully satisfies the bypass gate.","evidence":"Script lines 41-48: jq checks rule_id presence; grep -E checks the entry appears as a new '+' line in the diff. Neither check reads or compares expires_at against the current date. schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json defines expires_at (line 101, line 128) as 'type: string, minLength: 1' — no format constraint, no minimum-date constraint. The Python schema validation step (workflow lines 259-277) validates against schemas/waivers-file.schema.json which is not part of the 020B scope boundary and whose expires_at constraints are unknown; even if waivers-file.schema.json enforces ISO-8601 format, it does not compare the value to now(). The bypass gate is therefore satisfiable by adding a waiver entry that expired years ago.","impact":"An operator who legitimately obtained a waiver in the past (or a malicious adopter who pre-dates a waiver) can reuse an expired waiver to unlock the break-glass bypass. The waivers.json diff-membership check is satisfied (the expired waiver is added as a new line), the rule_id matches, the schema validates, and the bypass gate exits 0 — all while the waiver's authorisation window is long closed. The time-bounded nature of the waiver (the core governance control) is unenforced.","mitigation":"Add an expires_at validation step in verify-bypass-pairing.sh after the jq check: extract expires_at for the matching rule_id entry and compare it to the current UTC date using date -d and/or python3 -c. Fail with SCP-E004 if expires_at <= today. Also add 'format: date' and a pattern constraint ('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$') to expires_at in schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json for both disabled_rules and waivers_applied entries; this ensures downstream consumers (WP-SCP-023 aggregators) can parse dates reliably."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"verify-bypass-pairing.sh verifies that a D-NNN row was added to docs/DECISIONS.md but does not verify that the row references the bypass rule_id. A PR can add any unrelated D-NNN row (e.g., a legitimate architecture decision) to satisfy the governance gate while the waivers.json entry covers the actual bypass — the documentation trail is decoupled from the technical event.","evidence":"Script line 31: 'git diff --unified=0 ... -- docs/DECISIONS.md | grep -Eq '^\\+\\|\\s*D-0[0-9]{3}\\s*\\|\\s*20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\\s*\\|'' — the regex checks that some D-NNN table row was added. It does not grep for the specific rule_id (BYPASS_RULE_ID=$1), nor does it require any field in the row to contain the bypassed rule. The plan AC (viii-c)(2) states 'a sibling commit in the same PR contains both a docs/DECISIONS.md D-NNN record AND a matching waivers.json entry' — the intent is clear linkage, but the script does not enforce it. A PR that adds D-031 (some unrelated infra decision) and a waivers.json entry for SCP-R-001 satisfies both checks without the D-031 row mentioning SCP-R-001 at all.","impact":"The governance documentation trail for a break-glass event may be an unrelated D-NNN row that gives no indication a policy bypass occurred. Audit consumers (WP-SCP-023, future human auditors) who review DECISIONS.md for bypass evidence will not find it unless they also correlate waivers-applied records. The governance invariant that bypass events are traceable in DECISIONS.md is formally satisfied but semantically empty.","mitigation":"Extend the DECISIONS.md grep to also require the bypass rule_id to appear in the same added table row: after confirming the D-NNN row exists, run a second grep that combines both patterns, e.g., git diff ... -- docs/DECISIONS.md | grep -E '^\\+.*D-0[0-9]{3}' | grep -Fq \"${rule_id}\". This ensures the specific row added references the rule being bypassed. Additionally, document in the AC that the D-NNN row's description column must name the bypassed rule_id — the script can enforce presence, human review of the row content is the second control."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-004","severity":"MAJ","claim":"verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 46 interpolates the unescaped rule_id argument directly into a grep -E extended-regex pattern. A rule_id containing regex metacharacters changes the matching semantics; a rule_id of '.*' makes the grep match any line in the waivers diff that contains 'rule_id', bypassing the requirement that the specific rule appears as a newly-added entry.","evidence":"Script line 46: 'grep -Eq \"^\\+.*\\\"rule_id\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"${rule_id}\\\"\"'. The ${rule_id} is interpolated unescaped into the -E regex. Metacharacters .+?*|[]{}() in rule_id alter pattern semantics. Example: rule_id='.*' → pattern '^\\+.*\"rule_id\":\".*\"' which matches any added line containing 'rule_id' followed by any value — not just the target rule. Example: rule_id='SCP-R-001|SCP-R-002' → pattern becomes an alternation matching either rule. The BYPASS_RULE_ID is extracted from policy-findings.json via Python print() (workflow line 241) without sanitisation; if the policy evaluation (020C) is manipulated to produce a finding with a crafted rule_id, the regex is attacker-influenced. The jq call at line 41 correctly uses --arg rule_id (jq-safe), but the grep at line 46 does not.","impact":"With a manipulated policy evaluation producing a finding whose rule_id is '.*', the diff-membership check at line 46 accepts any waivers.json diff that contains any 'rule_id' key — not necessarily one matching the bypass rule. Combined with MAJ-BYPASS-003 (DECISIONS.md row not linked to rule_id), an attacker who can influence the policy output rule_id has full control over both bypass checks. The attack path requires compromising the policy evaluation step (020C scope), but the flaw in the script is present in 020B and will be live when 020C ships.","mitigation":"Use fgrep (grep -F, fixed-string match) instead of grep -E for the rule_id portion, or escape the rule_id before interpolation using printf '%s' \"${rule_id}\" | sed 's/[.^$*+?()[{|\\\\]/\\\\&/g'. Better: rewrite the diff check using jq for consistent semantics — pipe the waivers diff through jq to extract added rule_id values and compare literally: git diff ... -- \"${waivers_path}\" | grep '^+' | jq -Rs 'split(\"\\n\") | map(select(startswith(\"+\"))) | ...' | jq -e --arg rid \"${rule_id}\" 'any(.[]; . == $rid)'. This eliminates regex injection entirely."},{"id":"MAJ-BYPASS-005","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The 'Enforce break-glass pairing gates' step (if: inputs.scp_bypass) validates all three gates successfully but provides no mechanism to suppress the 'Render deny annotations and enforce threshold' step that unconditionally exits non-zero on deny findings. Break-glass is therefore operationally dead: a PR that satisfies all three gates still fails the required check, pushing operators toward disabling branch protection directly — a far more dangerous and unaudited bypass path.","evidence":"policy-check.yml: the bypass gate step at line 211 has condition 'if: inputs.scp_bypass'. If all three gates pass, the step exits 0 with no output variable or env-write that signals bypass approval. The 'Render deny annotations and enforce threshold' step at lines 301-336 has no 'if:' condition and always runs. Python at line 334: 'if denies and os.environ.get(\"SCP_THRESHOLD\") == \"deny\": sys.exit(1)' — SCP_BYPASS ('true') is never consulted. So a PR with scp_bypass=true that satisfies DECISIONS.md+waivers.json+schema produces: bypass gate exit 0, then threshold step exit 1, overall workflow exit 1, required check fails, merge blocked. Additionally: the bypass gate at lines 230-247 extracts BYPASS_RULE_ID from policy-findings.json and exits 1 if no deny finding exists — so scp_bypass=true with no deny findings also fails (the workflow fails when it would otherwise pass). The bypass input has no functional effect on any code path.","impact":"Any operator who follows the documented three-gate break-glass procedure and sets scp_bypass=true will see their PR fail anyway. Faced with a blocked emergency, they will likely: (a) ask to have the required check temporarily removed from branch protection, (b) push directly to main with admin override, or (c) create a dummy commit that forces the deny finding away. Options (a) and (b) are unaudited, don't produce the DECISIONS.md+waivers.json trail the system was designed to require, and leave no evidence in the policy artefacts. The break-glass design is sophisticated but the implementation makes it impossible to exercise — operators encounter a worse safety profile than if the bypass had never been designed.","mitigation":"After the bypass gate exits 0, write a step output or environment variable (e.g., echo 'SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED=true' >> $GITHUB_ENV). In the 'Render deny annotations and enforce threshold' step, check: 'if denies and os.environ.get(\"SCP_THRESHOLD\") == \"deny\" and os.environ.get(\"SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED\") != \"true\": sys.exit(1)'. This makes the threshold step respect a validated bypass. Additionally, emit a structured SCP-E004 annotation (already required by AC viii-b) only when the bypass is activated, to make bypass events visible in the PR timeline. Consider a dedicated summary line in the workflow summary stating 'BREAK-GLASS BYPASS ACTIVE — rule_id, expires_at, D-NNN ref' for audit visibility."},{"id":"MIN-BYPASS-006","severity":"MIN","claim":"schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json defines expires_at in both disabled_rules and waivers_applied as 'type: string, minLength: 1' with no format or pattern constraint. Any non-empty string passes schema validation. Downstream aggregators (WP-SCP-023) and the bypass gate's own schema validation will silently accept 'never', 'TBD', or '9999-99-99' as expires_at values.","evidence":"schema lines 99-103 (disabled_rules expires_at): 'type: string, minLength: 1'. Schema lines 128-130 (waivers_applied expires_at): identical. No 'format: date', no pattern '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$', no 'minimum' constraint. The Python schema validation in the bypass gate (workflow lines 259-277) validates waivers.json against schemas/waivers-file.schema.json, not this schema — but waivers-file.schema.json's expires_at constraints are outside the 020B scope boundary. The policy-check-summary.schema.json is the canonical consumer-facing schema per AC (x); its laxity sets the contract for all downstream processors.","impact":"WP-SCP-023 estate aggregators will receive summary artefacts with unparseable or semantically invalid expires_at values without schema-level rejection. A disabled rule with expires_at: 'indefinite' passes the schema, making the expiry field meaningless for automated tracking. The bypass-validity tracking (which depends on expires_at > today) becomes unreliable at the summary-artefact level. This is a MIN because the immediate gate check (in 020C.1) will be in the Rego waiver-aware logic, not the summary schema, but it establishes a bad contract.","mitigation":"Add 'format: date' and pattern '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$' to all expires_at fields in schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json. Add the same constraints to schemas/waivers-file.schema.json if it exists. Enable JSON Schema format validation (the default jsonschema library requires format_checker=jsonschema.FormatChecker() to enforce format keywords) in the Python validation step."},{"id":"MIN-BYPASS-007","severity":"MIN","claim":"The 'Collect changed files' step (policy-check.yml line 180) runs 'git diff --name-only SCP_BASE_SHA..SCP_HEAD_SHA' without error-code emission. If SCP_BASE_SHA is absent from the local git history (force-push deleted the base branch history; workflow triggered outside pull_request context; unusual merge-base scenarios), the git diff exits non-zero due to set -euo pipefail but emits no SCP-E001 annotation — an infra failure is indistinguishable from a policy deny in the PR UI.","evidence":"policy-check.yml lines 163-181: the 'Collect changed files' step emits a structured SCP-E001 error for missing SCP_BASE_SHA/SCP_HEAD_SHA env vars (lines 175-178) but not for a git-diff failure on a present-but-unreachable SHA. The git diff at line 180 runs directly without a surrounding 'emit_infra_failure' wrapper. The checkout step uses fetch-depth: 0 (full history) which mitigates most shallow-clone scenarios, but force-push to the base branch between PR open and workflow run can still cause the base SHA to be garbage-collected or missing. The step exits with git's exit code, which the workflow surfaces as a generic step failure without an SCP-EXXX title.","impact":"Operators see a failing required check with no SCP-E001 annotation. They cannot distinguish a git infrastructure failure (retry/contact owner) from a genuine policy deny (fix code). Workflow log inspection is required to identify the root cause. This is MIN severity because the PR is correctly blocked (merge-blocked is the safe outcome) but the error UX violates AC (viii-b) which mandates named error codes for infra failures.","mitigation":"Wrap the git diff call at line 180 in a subshell with explicit error handling: 'git diff --name-only \"${SCP_BASE_SHA}..${SCP_HEAD_SHA}\" > changed-files.txt || emit_infra_failure \"git diff failed: base SHA ${SCP_BASE_SHA} may not exist in local history (force-push or non-PR context)\"'. The emit_infra_failure function already exists in this step's scope (defined at lines 168-172) and emits SCP-E001 before exiting."},{"id":"nit-BYPASS-008","severity":"nit","claim":"verify-bypass-pairing.sh uses grep -Fxq (fixed-string exact-line match) to check whether waivers_path appears in the git diff output. The git diff --name-only output always omits the leading './' prefix. A caller who passes waivers-path: ./output/findings/waivers.json (note leading ./) will fail the diff-membership check even when the file was correctly modified in the PR, because './output/findings/waivers.json' != 'output/findings/waivers.json'.","evidence":"Script line 26: 'grep -Fxq \"${waivers_path}\" <<<\"${changed_files}\"'. The changed_files variable is populated by 'git diff --name-only base..HEAD' which emits paths as 'output/findings/waivers.json' (no leading './'). The waivers_path variable is set from SCP_WAIVERS_PATH which comes from the workflow input 'waivers-path'. The default value in the workflow ('output/findings/waivers.json') has no leading './' and works correctly. But the input description does not prohibit './output/findings/waivers.json', which a reasonable caller might supply. The -Fx flag means the mismatch silently causes a confusing SCP-E004 failure: 'output/findings/waivers.json must be part of the bypass diff' even though the file is visibly in the diff.","impact":"Minimal — the operator adjusts their caller wrapper. But the error message says the file is not in the diff when it actually is, creating a misleading debugging experience. Nit severity because the default value works and the AC does not require './' support.","mitigation":"Normalise waivers_path before the grep: 'waivers_path=\"${waivers_path#./}\"' (strip leading './' if present). One line, no dependencies."}],"self_reported_concerns":["CRIT-BYPASS-001 (Conftest vendor binary without SHA256) is unambiguous from code inspection. The other findings assume the policy-findings.json is populated by an honest OPA/Conftest evaluation; in the 020B scaffold state, policy-findings.json is always [] (no Rego rules yet per slice scope), meaning the bypass gate always fails (no deny findings to extract BYPASS_RULE_ID from). MAJ-BYPASS-004 and MAJ-BYPASS-005 matter critically once 020C ships real rules — the 020B code will be live at that point unchanged.","MAJ-BYPASS-005 (bypass gate non-functional) is the finding most likely to cause governance harm at operational time, because it forces legitimate break-glass users toward unsafe workarounds. The other MAJ findings (002, 003, 004) require attacker-controlled inputs or are exploitable only with compromised policy evaluation. MAJ-005 manifests for any operator who follows the documented procedure.","The schemas/waivers-file.schema.json referenced at workflow line 270 is outside the 020B scope boundary and was not reviewed. Its expires_at constraints (or lack thereof) directly affect the completeness of MAJ-BYPASS-002. This finding should be re-evaluated once waivers-file.schema.json is committed."]
